text:
Alice M.: heads up — our Next.js middleware that talks to the JS SDK is crashing in the canary. stack shows `TypeError: setTimeout is not a function` when the token refresh path runs
Ben K.: repro'd locally on Next 13.4 edge runtime. it only happens when the client tries to start a refresh timer inside middleware (so during the request lifecycle)
Carol S.: yep — edge runtimes (Vercel/Next edge) don't expose the traditional timers the SDK expects. setTimeout/setInterval are not available in that environment by design.
Alice M.: bummer. we can't move refresh out of middleware easily because we need to mint a short-lived access token before proxying to the backend. any safe workaround?
Dave L.: tried polyfilling `globalThis.setTimeout = (...args) => queueMicrotask(() => args[0]())` but that broke expected delays and made retry backoffs immediate. not acceptable. also saw a couple of ESM/CJS import issues when bundling the SDK for edge — `require(...)` fails inside middleware.
Carol S.: concrete options, ordered by safety:
1) avoid timers in middleware: perform a synchronous check using token expiry metadata (exp) and call a /refresh endpoint if token near-expiry. this avoids scheduling.
2) implement a tiny refresh proxy route (standard SSR/edge route) that is executed server-side (not middleware) and have middleware call it quickly if needed.
3) polyfill carefully: only microtask polyfills make sense for immediate defers, but not for timeouts. avoid if semantics matter.

Alice M.: can you paste example of option (1)?
Carol S.: sure — example middleware pattern that is edge friendly:

```
// middleware.ts (edge)
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference-js'

export default async function middleware(req) {
  const client = createClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY, runtime: 'edge' });
  const cookie = req.headers.get('cookie') || '';

  // call a tiny refresh endpoint that returns a short-lived token (stateless)
  const refreshRes = await fetch(new URL('/api/refresh', req.url), { method: 'POST', body: cookie });
  if (!refreshRes.ok) return NextResponse.rewrite(new URL('/auth', req.url));

  const body = await refreshRes.json();
  const access = body.access;

  const res = NextResponse.next();
  res.headers.set('authorization', `Bearer ${access}`);
  return res;
}
```

This avoids using setTimeout in the middleware entirely.
Ben K.: that looks reasonable. small caveat: our refresh endpoint must be extremely fast (it runs inline). we had been using the SDK's `client.auth.refresh()` which internally relied on a timer for retries/backoff.
Eli R.: FYI I opened a small SDK patch that makes the client avoid timers in edge runtime and fall back to immediate errors + TTL checks. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1234 (edge-friendly refresh mode). it also exports an explicit `runtime: 'edge'` hint for createClient so bundlers can tree-shake node-only bits.
Alice M.: awesome. can we get a patch release? this blocks a couple customers.
Eli R.: i'll cut a patch (v0.12.3) after tests. it replaces setTimeout-based retry with a non-timer loop that uses response TTL and explicit retry headers when present. still warns if you try to use exponential backoff in edge.
Dave L.: separate but related: TypeScript types in edge middleware were noisy — `NextRequest` vs standard `Request`. adding an explicit cast fixes a lot:

```
import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server'
export default async function middleware(req: NextRequest) { ... }
```

or if you must, `const nr = req as NextRequest;` to satisfy the SDK helper overloads.
Carol S.: also watch your bundler target. if you're using next's default edge build, make sure SDK is imported as ESM. avoid `require(...)` and CommonJS entrypoints. prefer:

```
import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference-js'
```

not `const { createClient } = require('redwood-inference')` — that breaks on edge.
Alice M.: thanks all. we'll try the v0.12.3 patch and migrate our middleware to call /api/refresh as an interim fix. will report back if anything else pops up.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout 3/4 hosts passed :rocket:
Ben K.: follow-up note — document this pattern in devex README and maybe add a small example in the SDK repo (edge-middleware.md). i've opened a follow-up issue.
Alice M.: logged. thanks everyone :heart:
